title: Words as coordinates: king minus man plus woman
summary: A 2013 paper showed that king minus man plus woman lands closest to queen in a word vector space. A 2020 paper argued analogies are not an accurate test for bias.

beats.say: King minus man plus woman lands closest to queen, in a model.
A model can turn each word into a list of numbers.
That list works like coordinates, a position on a map.
A Google paper trained word vectors on one point six billion words, in under a day.
The paper's example: king minus man plus woman is closest to queen.
On the paper's relationship test, its best skip-gram model scored sixty five point six percent.
A later paper argued analogies are not an accurate test for bias.
Its title: Man is to doctor as woman is to doctor.
beats.cap: "Man is to doctor as woman is to doctor"

beats.say: The vectors are real. The tidy example is not the whole picture.
Words became positions, and positions can be added.

claims.note: Mikolov et al. abstract: high quality word vectors learned from a 1.6 billion word data set in less than a day
Mikolov et al., Table 6: Skip-gram 1000-dim trained on 6B words, total accuracy 65.6% on the Semantic-Syntactic Word Relationship test set

facts.claim: Mikolov, Chen, Corrado and Dean (Google) learned word vectors from a 1.6 billion word data set in under a day, and vector('King') - vector('Man') + vector('Woman') is closest to vector('Queen')
facts.note: arXiv 1301.3781: abstract and the vector-offset example

facts.claim: The best skip-gram model in the paper reached 65.6% total accuracy on the Semantic-Syntactic Word Relationship test
facts.note: arXiv 1301.3781, Table 6: 1000-dim, 6B words: 66.1% semantic, 65.1% syntactic, 65.6% total

facts.claim: A 2020 Computational Linguistics paper titled 'Fair Is Better than Sensational: Man Is to Doctor as Woman Is to Doctor' argues analogies are not an accurate diagnostic for bias
facts.note: ACL Anthology 2020.cl-2.7 abstract: 'analogies are in fact not an accurate diagnostic for bias'; human biases are still present in embeddings
